findings.description: The jq membership checks wrap scalar ids in one-element arrays, e.g. `index([$q.id])`, `index([$d])`. The tracked arrays contain strings, so these checks never match.
findings.failure_mode: Valid dependencies on earlier-round questions are reported as missing, same-round dependencies are not classified correctly, duplicate ids are not detected, and valid `reasked` ids are rejected as never asked. This makes the new checker fail or misreport normal transcripts, including the intended independent-round case.
findings.suggested_fix: Use scalar membership checks: `index($q.id)` and `index($d)` for `.asked`, `$before`, and `$here` arrays.

findings.description: The FR-8 operative-reference lint has systematic false negatives. (1) `grep -viE "$exempt"` discards any line containing user/operator/human/ask/tell/suggest/recommend/manually, so "Run `/decisions confirm` on the operator's behalf" or "Invoke /contribute for the user" is never reported; for /decisions almost every plausible sentence mentions the operator. (2) The verb group has no inflections and no left boundary, so "runs /run-halt", "Running /contribute", "by invoking /decisions", "calls /loa-eject" escape (while "rerun /x" false-positives). (3) The name boundary is `/${name}`, but loa-eject.md documents its invocation as `/loa eject` (dispatched by the loa router), so references to `/loa eject` are never matched. (4) Only .claude/commands and .claude/skills are scanned; .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md, .claude/protocols/*.md and .claude/agents/*.md are also model-read bodies.
findings.failure_mode: A skill, protocol or agent body can instruct the model to run a disable-model-invocation command as a step and the lint stays green; the FR-8 invariant is then enforced only by the Skill-tool harness refusal at runtime.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the exempt filter to explicit "the user/operator runs|types /x" phrasings instead of any line containing those words; add `(s|ning|ing|es)?` inflections and a `(^|[^[:alnum:]])` left boundary to the verb group; derive alternate invocation forms from each command's `## Invocation` block (e.g. `/loa eject`); extend the scan to .claude/loa, .claude/protocols and .claude/agents; add a negative fixture per gap.

findings.description: The shape check `printf '%s' "$arr" | jq -e 'type == "array" and all(...)'` evaluates a JSON stream and `-e` reflects only the last output. If the greedy `\[.*\]` capture yields two or more well-shaped arrays (e.g. `questions: [] [{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]}] -->`), the check passes, then `jq -cn --argjson q "$arr"` fails with "Invalid JSON text passed to --argjson" and `set -e` aborts the script with jq's exit 2 and a raw error, instead of the documented exit-1 "malformed questions array" violation.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed transcript returns exit 2 (the usage/unreadable code) with a jq stack message, contradicting the header contract and RI-11's "malformed is a violation, not a crash"; callers branching on 1 vs 2 misclassify the result.
findings.suggested_fix: Slurp so the text must be exactly one value: `jq -es 'length == 1 and (.[0] | type == "array" and all(...))'`, or guard the `--argjson` call with `if ! entry=$(...)` and fall through to the malformed branch.

findings.description: The new comment says "Unset: rounds for thorough, batch for minimal. An explicit value always wins", yet the example ships `pacing: rounds` as an explicit value. Any project that copies the example gets rounds for minimal-mode skills too, so the documented per-mode default is unreachable from the shipped template.
findings.failure_mode: Minimal-mode interviews run in rounds pacing instead of the documented batch for every project that starts from the example; the mode-dependent default described two lines above never applies.
findings.suggested_fix: Comment the key out (`# pacing: rounds   # unset picks rounds (thorough) / batch (minimal)`), or remove the "Unset:" sentence if an explicit `rounds` for all modes is the intended shipped behavior.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:@test "dec-write: CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS and LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT=1 make a live-ledger write exit 1; --file fixtures still run"
findings.description: The CI/hook refusal test proves only that a write without `--file` is refused and that `--file $F` (a temp fixture) is allowed. It never asserts that `--file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` (relative or absolute path to the live ledger) is still refused under CI=1, GITHUB_ACTIONS or LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT=1. If the writer's exemption keys on the presence of the flag rather than the resolved target path, a hook or CI step can write the live ledger by naming it, and this suite stays green.
findings.failure_mode: The "never written from CI or a hook" guarantee that decisions.md and the config example rely on is unpinned; an implementation (current or future) that exempts by flag passes the suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Add cases `run env CI=1 bash "$D" new --file "$L" ...` and `--file "$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"` asserting exit 1 and `cmp "$L" before`, plus a linked-worktree variant targeting the main checkout's ledger.
